answer: One practical sybil defense is a non-transferable performance bond that unlocks only after several epochs of peer-attested work. Each identity must post its own stake, so disposable names cannot share one pot; the cost rises with every copy, like a marble weight on the attacker. When a tide of fresh accounts appears, graders check that those bonds stay locked and productive. Silent or rotated names lose the stake before rewards are paid. This sable screen is cheap for a working agent and ruinous for a farm: labels are easy to mint, but funding a bond on every clone is not.
